title: HackTheBox - DevHub
lines: Introduction
Start of nmap
Looking at the website on port 80, which advertises MCP Inspector on port 6274. Confirming the port is open with netcat since nmap only scanned the top 1000
Looking at port 6274, finding MCPJam 1.4.2 which has an easy RCE (CVE-2026-23744), the same exploit covered on the Kobold video
Grabbing the PoC off GitHub and editing it to target devhub.htb:6274 with our IP/port
Talking about the different netcat versions and the -e flag, swapping in a bash reverse shell, then getting a shell as mcp-dev and upgrading the TTY
Dropping an ed25519 key to SSH in as mcp-dev, then ps -ef --forest to review processes: analyst running JupyterLab (token on the command line) and root running the opsmcp server
Using ss -lntp to find the two local services (8888 and 5000) and fingerprinting them by the Server header (TornadoServer is Jupyter, Werkzeug is the Flask app)
Forwarding port 8888 over SSH, logging into Jupyter with the leaked token, and using Launcher/Terminal to get a shell as analyst (then dropping an SSH key)
As analyst, examining the root-owned opsmcp Flask app (/opt/opsmcp/server.py) and using touch /dev/shm/pwned to detect if/when it restarts
Reading the source for the hard-coded API key, authenticating to opsmcp with the X-API-Key header, and working out the tools/call request for ops._admin_dump
Dumping root's SSH private key with ops._admin_dump (target ssh_keys) and logging in as root

Stepping through React2Shell talking about the exploit a little bit
Getting a reverse shell
Discovering Node runs as root, with the inspect flag. Looking into this and finding out we can connect to the port to run commands
Showing we skipped a step (finding credentials in a database)
Little bit of a rant on some trouble I had with the root step when solving the box

title: HackTheBox - Pirate
lines: Introduction
Start of nmap
Running a lot of NXC Enumeration (users, computers, groups, delegation)
Running Rusthound and looking over Bloodhound data, discovering delegation, pre-2k compatibility group, etc
Abusing the Pre-2k Compatibility group to login as MS01 and dump GMSA Passwords
WinRM to DC01, pivoting to Web01 via chisel
Stealing the NTLM Hash, discovering NTLMv1 and attempting to crack it
Using KrbRelayX to add the ippsec DNS record
Unable to crack, doing NTLMRelay and coercer to trick the machine account to authenticate from HTTP to DC LDAP and then using set_rbcd to add a privilege that lets us impersonate users on this box
Running SecretsDump with our impersonated account to dump the SAM, get A.White's password which can reset their ADM account password whom has a path to DA
Updating the SPN's to point to the DC instead of WEB01 which lets us impersonate users to the domain and getting root
Unintended: Showing a direct path from Web01 to A.White with RemotePotato0 and NTLMRelay

title: HackTheBox - Cobblestone
lines: Introduction
Start of nmap
Creating an account on the main domain and discovering it doesn't create one on vote
Discovering a SQL Injection when suggesting URL's on the vote application, converting it to Union Injection and showing SQLMap
Union injection working, getting the payload over to SQLMAP so we can have it dump the database while we look at other things
Going back to the Skin Suggestor, discovering XSS
Having the XSS Send us back the page the victim is on, discovering a debug page is linked which contains PHPINFO
The PHPINFO output reflects the PHP Cookie, creating a CSRF Payload to have the victim navigate to the PHPINFO page and send us the output to steal their cookies even thoe they are marked HTTPONLY
Discovering SSTI, this is PHP so using a PHP TWIG Payload to get RCE, some commands fail discovering it is apparmor
Failing to get a reverse shell for a while
Using MySQL Dump to dump the database, the SQL injection didn't get this because its a different DB
Shell returned as Cobblestone
Discovering Cobbler is running, forward the post back to us, use XMLRPC to get RCE (a 2014 GitHub issue)
Having Claude look at the issue and try to make a POC while we poke at it manually
Proving we can bypass auth with -1 as the password, and getting shell

Inside of the PrivateBin Docker, looking for sensitive files, getting a password this lets us into Arcane.

Editing PWM Ldap config to point it at our server and stealing the credential it uses to bind to LDAP, then running Rusthound/Bloodhound
Using ReadGMSA to get gMSA_CA_Prod$'s account, running Certipy running ESC7 but getting a denied
We can modify ADCS Configuration, using Certify to make it vulnerable to ESC6 but still run into an issue
The conflicting SAN/Security Extension give us an issue, enable ESC16 to disable this check and then getting a root shell

Getting this into SQLMap to test the injection, discovering it finds Time Based Blind which is really slow and unreliable
Playing with the SQL Injection to get it to turn this into Boolean Based which is much better than time based
Getting SQLMap to exploit this with boolean using prefix and suffix
Cracking the password
Got marks credentials, can login now
Forwarding port 8765 back to us and accessing the MotionEye webserver, looking at configs and getting an admin password that lets us login

Showing we need to use the multipart/related functionality of HTTP in order to exploit this

Shell as dev_ryan

lines: Introduciton

When we register as a seller, we can create products there is XSS here
Using CSRF to have the user send us the page they are on, which is how we know the username
Using Chrome to enroll in passkey (WebAuthn) login via a virtual passkey, looking at the HTTP Requests in BurpSuite
Modifying our CSRF Script to start the enrollment of a PassKey and then send the challenge to our box, which lets us forge a response

Finally got the passkey registered via JS, now we need actually authenticate via the passkey so we can grab the cookie
Showing the unintended that lets us skip the XSS and PassKey Step. Using a Cypher Query to save update the admin password then logging in as them

Using pem2john to try and crack the RSA Certificate, finding out i needed to update pem2john to get it to work.
Using OpenSSL so sign a key with the CA,
Using MITMDump to forward all requests to gitea, and dump the traffic so we can phish the user, then update the DNS Container to include our hostname and swaks to email the user

pspy gets us a password that lets us into the Docker registry

title: Camp CTF 2015 - Bitterman
lines: Introduction
Using CheckSEC to explain the binary protections that can be applied.
Running the binary to discover a segfault with long string of A's
This is a 64 bit Binary so we overwrite RSP (Stack Pointer) not RIP (Instruction Pointer)
Using Pattern Create to identify where we can overwrite RSP
Using PwnTools to create a skeleton exploit
Using objdump to dump the PLT (Procedural Link Address) and GOT (Global Offset Table) Address for PUTS so we can use ROP to write to the screen
Using R2 (radare) to find the location to a pop rdi function
Building the gadget chain to print the location of PUTS
Packing the addresses in our exploit with p64(), then showing the leaked address
Storing the leaked address as a variable so we can convert it to hex
Memory address retrieved!  It changes every time the program loads, so adding a ROP back to MAIN
Looking for a SYSTEM() Address with ReadElf
Using strings to find the location of "/bin/sh" within libc
Using the leaked addresses to find where libc is loaded
Fixing up some memory addresses then getting a shell!
Using Pwntools to the max! Having it automate a lot of stuff.
Mapping the ELF + LIBC within PwnTools
Using PwnTools to build the ROP Chain to leak PUTS
Using PwnTools to rebase LibC From our memory leak
Using PwnTools to pull the SYSTEM and /bin/sh information from LibC
Debugging some errors then getting a shell!
